claim: When Systems Manager uses AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints), traffic between managed instances, Systems Manager and Amazon EC2 stays on the Amazon network, the managed instances don't have access to the Internet, and you don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device or a virtual private gateway.
question: Can interface VPC endpoints replace a NAT gateway for Systems Manager (Session Manager) on an instance in a private subnet?

values.display: don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device
values.spoken: no internet gateway and no NAT gateway needed

values.display: managed instances don't have access to the Internet
values.spoken: the instances have no internet access

qualifiers.scope: Systems Manager managed instances that use interface VPC endpoints
qualifiers.condition: interface VPC endpoints for Systems Manager are configured

evidence.quote: AWS PrivateLink restricts all network traffic between your managed instances, Systems Manager, and Amazon EC2 to the Amazon network. This means that your managed instances don't have access to the Internet. If you use AWS PrivateLink, you don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device, or a virtual private gateway.

claim: Without a VPC endpoint, Systems Manager managed instances need outbound internet access and must allow HTTPS (port 443) outbound traffic to the Systems Manager endpoints listed on the page; SSM Agent initiates all connections to the Systems Manager service, so you don't need to allow inbound traffic to your instances for Systems Manager.
question: What network path does the SSM Agent need for Session Manager when there are no VPC endpoints, and does the instance need an open inbound port?

values.spoken: outbound HTTPS on port four forty-three

values.display: allow inbound traffic to your instances

qualifiers.scope: Systems Manager managed instances without VPC endpoints
qualifiers.condition: outbound internet access is used instead of a VPC endpoint
